title: Safer Defaults in Rust
description: A mostly-sound helper that reads one input and formats a greeting. It shows a minor hardening point: unchecked length and unused Result.

finding.title: Missing Input Validation (Informational)
finding.description: The default memory safety of Rust helps here, but user input is trusted without a size or content bound.
finding.why_dangerous: Any externally supplied input should be assumed hostile even when memory is safe.
finding.impact: Where there is low; an unvalidated value can feed other sinks and cause injection or logical failures.
finding.fix: Validate length and content with an allowlist before use.
learning_example: Memory-safe languages still need input validation
Validate at the boundary, not deep inside the logic

checklist: Validate all external input even in memory-safe languages
Use the language's safe abstractions (String, Vec) over raw pointers
Review security sensors for informational findings too
